S06-native.title: Week 1 roadmap: Find C, Travel, Add a voice
S06-native.desc: Three steps in order: 1 Find C, 2 Travel, 3 Add a voice. Below, a keyboard drawing with brackets over the groups of two, three and two black keys; both Cs are highlighted, each the white key just left of a group of two black keys.

A01-native.title: One note on a keyboard
A01-native.desc: A short run of six white keys with one key highlighted and no letters. One sound only: not a chord, not a scale.

A02-native.title: Pitch versus loudness
A02-native.desc: Top: seven white keys; a key and the key to its right are highlighted, with lower to the left and higher to the right. Bottom: the same key played softer and louder, shown as small and large ripples. Higher or lower depends on which key; louder or softer depends on how hard you press.

A03-native.title: Finding C from the black keys
A03-native.desc: Ten white keys. Black keys sit in a group of two, then three, then two, marked 2, 3, 2. The white key just left of each group of two is C; both Cs are highlighted.

A03-narrow.title: Finding C (narrow layout)
A03-narrow.desc: Eight white keys with groups of two and three black keys marked; the first and last white keys are C, highlighted.

A05-native.title: Seven names, then C again
A05-native.desc: Eight white keys numbered 1 to 8 with the letters C D E F G A B C. The first and last are both C. There is no black key between E and F or between B and C.

A05-narrow.title: Seven names, then C again (narrow layout)
A05-narrow.desc: Eight numbered white keys lettered C D E F G A B C.

A07-native.title: Up and back down from C to C
A07-native.desc: Two copies of the same eight white keys. First numbered 1 to 8 from the left C to the right C, going up. Second numbered 1 to 8 from the right C back to the left C, going down.

A06-native.title: Two Cs, one octave apart
A06-native.desc: Eight white keys. The left-most and right-most are both C and highlighted, joined by an arc labelled one octave up. The right one is higher.

A08-native.title: Two endings: away from C and home to C
A08-native.desc: Two keyboards. Version 1 plays the white keys C D E F G in order and stops on G. Version 2 plays C D E D C and stops on C, the home note. Practice example only.

A09-native.title: A note that stays while others visit
A09-native.desc: Three timelines of six seconds. In each, C sounds the whole time on the lower line, while one visiting note (E, then G, then D in the three examples) sounds from about 1 to 4.5 seconds on the upper line.

A10-native.title: A tiny melody with a pause (example)
A10-native.desc: An example idea in four boxes and a dashed pause: C, D, E, pause, C. A keyboard shows the first three keys. This is an example; learners choose their own notes.

A11-native.title: Your own sound-to-colour map
A11-native.desc: Three empty dashed circles labelled sound 1, sound 2 and sound 3, each with two blank writing lines. Your own sound-to-colour interpretation: there is no fixed colour for any note.

A12-native.title: Lesson 1A recap
A12-native.desc: Four small panels. 1: the two-then-three black-key pattern with both Cs highlighted. 2: the white keys C to the next C, one octave. 3: C at the centre with D E F G A B around it, chosen as home in this exercise. 4: a twelve-second timeline where the lower C is held while the upper voice visits E, G and D.

B01-early.title: Seven rising notes, unfinished
B01-early.desc: Seven white keys numbered 1 to 7 with the letters C D E F G A B, played one at a time. The path stops on the seventh note.

B01-pair.title: Same beginning, different last note
B01-pair.desc: Two keyboards. Ending 1 plays C D E F G A B and stops on B. Ending 2 plays the same seven notes and then adds the higher C, highlighted as home. Only the second adds the higher C.

B02-native.title: Where the half steps really are
B02-native.desc: Three keyboard pieces, each one semitone: E to F (two white keys with no black key between them), B to C (also no black key between), and C to C sharp (a white key and the black key right next to it).

B03-native.title: A whole step is two semitones
B03-native.desc: Left: C to D passes through the black key C sharp, two one-semitone hops, a whole step. Right: E to F sharp passes through F, also two semitones.

B04-native.title: One white-key move, two real distances
B04-native.desc: Left: C to D crosses one black key, so it is 2 semitones. Right: E to F has no black key between them, so it is 1 semitone. Each move is one white key, but the distances differ.

B05-native.title: C major: whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half
B05-native.desc: Eight white keys C to C. Arcs between neighbouring scale notes are labelled W for a whole step of 2 semitones or H for a half step of 1: W W H W W W H. The half steps are E to F and B to C.

B06-native.title: Seven names and the next C
B06-native.desc: Eight white keys numbered 1 to 8 lettered C D E F G A B C; the first and last are both C.

B09-native.title: Closeness versus measured distance
B09-native.desc: Left: C to C sharp is 1 semitone, the very next key. Right: C to D is 2 semitones. The painted arcs are only decoration; the numbered hops on the real keys are the measurement.

B10-native.title: Make an open ending and an arrival
B10-native.desc: Two keyboards sharing the opening C D E: one ends on G, the other ends on C. Authored practice patterns, not a lesson recording.

B11-native.title: The same pattern from G (optional)
B11-native.desc: Eight white keys starting on G. The same whole-whole-half-whole-whole-whole-half arcs, with the seventh note the black key F sharp. Optional enrichment.

C01-native.title: A held lower C with three visiting notes
C01-native.desc: Twelve-second timeline. Lower voice: C for the whole 12 seconds. Upper voice: E from 2 to 4 seconds, G from 5 to 7, D from 9 to 11.

C02-native.title: Two distinct voices
C02-native.desc: A timeline of the lower voice holding C while the upper voice plays E, G, D, and below it a keyboard showing the lower C and the upper notes D, E and G further to the right.

C03-native.title: Lower and higher voice positions
C03-native.desc: Fourteen white keys. The lower voice is the highlighted C on the left. The upper voice is the highlighted D, E and G further right.

C04-native.title: Early versus late entrance
C04-native.desc: Two twelve-second timelines with the lower C held throughout. In the first, the upper E plays from 2 to 6 seconds. In the second, the same E plays from 7 to 11 seconds. Only the entrance time differs.

C05-native.title: Time as a musical relationship
C05-native.desc: Twelve-second timeline with one-second ticks. Lower C 0 to 12. Upper E 2 to 4, G 5 to 7, D 9 to 11.

C06-native.title: One voice alone, then both together
C06-native.desc: Three twelve-second timelines using the same events: the lower C alone, the upper notes E, G and D alone, and both together.

C07-native.title: The same 36 seconds, two endings
C07-native.desc: Two 36-second timelines with the same held lower C and the same upper notes E, G, D, B. The second adds one extra upper note, a higher C from 33 to 35.8 seconds.

C08-native.title: Silence as space
C08-native.desc: The twelve-second example with the upper voice resting between its notes: 0 to 2, 4 to 5, 7 to 9 and 11 to 12 seconds, shown as dashed boxes labelled rest, while the lower C keeps sounding.

C09-native.title: Compose a two-voice story: worksheet
C09-native.desc: Five numbered boxes with writing lines: 1 Set a scene, 2 Imagine a visitor, 3 Leave some room, 4 Change something, 5 Choose an ending. Below, eight white keys lettered C to C for reference.

C10-native.title: Week 1 soundscape map
C10-native.desc: The twelve-second example: lower C held, upper E, G, D visiting. Caption: the lower line stayed, the upper line changed; Week 2 moves the lower line as well.

S07-native.title: Two Voices: Week 2 roadmap
S07-native.desc: Heading Two Voices, then a four-step roadmap: a pair, the interval, movement, changed support.

D01-native.title: C and E together: a dyad
D01-native.desc: Five white keys B C D E F. C is highlighted as the lower voice and E as the upper voice.

D02-native.title: The two keys: C and E
D02-native.desc: Three white keys C D E with C and E highlighted and D between them.

D03-native.title: C to E is four semitones
D03-native.desc: Three white keys with the two black keys between them. Four numbered hops carry C to E through C sharp, D and D sharp. Four semitones, a major third.

D04-native.title: C to E compared with C to F
D04-native.desc: Left: C to E counts four semitones, a major third. Right: C to F counts five semitones, a perfect fourth.

D05-native.title: Hold C, move E up to F
D05-native.desc: Two keyboards: C and E, then C and F. The lower C stays; the upper voice rises one semitone from E to F.

D06-native.title: Hold E, move the lower C
D06-native.desc: Two examples. First C and E become B and E: the lower voice falls one semitone. Second C and E become D and E: the lower voice rises two semitones. The upper E stays.

D07-native.title: Two voices across five seconds
D07-native.desc: Lower voice: C for the whole five seconds. Upper voice: E from 0 to 2.5 seconds, then F from 2.5 to 5.

D09-native.title: Try three dyads
D09-native.desc: Three practice pairs, each starting from C and E: upper E to F, lower C to B, lower C to D.

D10-native.title: Lesson 2A recap
D10-native.desc: An interval is counted in semitones: C to E is four, C to F is five. Then one voice moves while the other stays: C and E become C and F.

E01-native.title: One beginning, five changes
E01-native.desc: Five endings that all start from C and E: C and F, B and E, D and E, B and F, D and F. They show three kinds of motion: oblique, contrary and similar.

E02-native.title: Oblique motion: one voice holds
E02-native.desc: Three examples where one voice stays and the other moves: upper E up to F; lower C down to B; lower C up to D.

E03-native.title: Contrary motion: moving apart
E03-native.desc: C and E become B and F: the lower voice falls and the upper voice rises. B to F is six semitones, a diminished fifth (tritone).

E04-native.title: Similar motion: rising together
E04-native.desc: C and E become D and F: the lower voice rises two semitones and the upper voice rises one. D to F is three semitones, a minor third.

E07-native.title: All five examples, three kinds of motion
E07-native.desc: Five rows, each from C and E: B1 upper rises (oblique), B2 lower falls (oblique), B3 lower rises (oblique), B4 both move apart (contrary), B5 both rise (similar).

E08-native.title: B to F: the tritone lens
E08-native.desc: Five white keys B C D E F. B and F are highlighted; six numbered hops cross the black keys between them. Five letter names, six semitones: a diminished fifth, also called a tritone.

E09-native.title: A conversation in four stages
E09-native.desc: Four keyboards in order: C and E, C and F, B and F, then back to C and E. Each stage lasts two and a half seconds.

E10-native.title: Four moments on a timeline
E10-native.desc: Ten-second timeline. Lower voice: C 0 to 5, B 5 to 7.5, C 7.5 to 10. Upper voice: E 0 to 2.5, F 2.5 to 7.5, E 7.5 to 10.

E11-native.title: Compose a two-voice conversation
E11-native.desc: An example of four stages (C and E, C and F, B and F, C and E), then two blank dashed lanes for your own lower and upper voices to sketch.

F01-native.title: Same upper melody, two foundations
F01-native.desc: Two 36-second timelines with the identical upper line E (4 to 10), F (14 to 20), E (26 to 32). In situation 1 the lower voice holds C throughout. In situation 2 it plays C for 0 to 12, B for 12 to 24 and C for 24 to 36.

F04-native.title: Shared and only-here notes at the F moment
F04-native.desc: Labels over the two overlapping fields. Left: C, only in situation 1. Centre overlap: F, shared by both. Right: B, only in situation 2.

F05-native.title: Objective change versus personal response
F05-native.desc: Two columns. Left, what changes: the upper melody is identical, only the lower voice differs. Right, an open question: how did that feel to you? No right answer.

F06-native.title: Two versions aligned in time
F06-native.desc: Two registered 36-second timelines with the same upper line and a shaded band over 14 to 20 seconds, the F moment. Empty upper-voice parts are marked as rests while the lower voice may still sound.

F07-native.title: C to F versus B to F
F07-native.desc: Left: C to F is five semitones, a perfect fourth. Right: B to F is six semitones, a diminished fifth or tritone. The melody note F is the same in both.

F08-native.title: A two-voice dialogue (optional practice path)
F08-native.desc: Four keyboards in order: C and E, C and F, B and F, C and E, two seconds each. An optional path to play and then change.

F09-native.title: One melody in two contexts
F09-native.desc: Three moments of the melody, E then F then E, in each situation. Upper notes are identical. Lower voice: situation 1 is C, C, C; situation 2 is C, B, C.

F10-native.title: Week 2 recap: three anchors
F10-native.desc: Three small panels: C to E is four semitones; a four-stage motion C+E, C+F, B+F, C+E; and two situations sharing only the note F.

T07-IP-00.title: Perfect unison: 0 semitones
T07-IP-00.desc: Perfect unison (P1), C and C, 0 semitones apart, 1 letter names.

T08-IP-00.title: Atlas chapter IP-00: Perfect unison
T08-IP-00.desc: Chapter opening for Perfect unison: 0 semitones, C to C.

T07-IP-01.title: Minor second: 1 semitones
T07-IP-01.desc: Minor second (m2), C and D♭, 1 semitones apart, 2 letter names.

T08-IP-01.title: Atlas chapter IP-01: Minor second
T08-IP-01.desc: Chapter opening for Minor second: 1 semitones, C to D♭.

T07-IP-02.title: Major second: 2 semitones
T07-IP-02.desc: Major second (M2), C and D, 2 semitones apart, 2 letter names.

T08-IP-02.title: Atlas chapter IP-02: Major second
T08-IP-02.desc: Chapter opening for Major second: 2 semitones, C to D.

T07-IP-03.title: Minor third: 3 semitones
T07-IP-03.desc: Minor third (m3), C and E♭, 3 semitones apart, 3 letter names.

T08-IP-03.title: Atlas chapter IP-03: Minor third
T08-IP-03.desc: Chapter opening for Minor third: 3 semitones, C to E♭.

T07-IP-04.title: Major third: 4 semitones
T07-IP-04.desc: Major third (M3), C and E, 4 semitones apart, 3 letter names.

T08-IP-04.title: Atlas chapter IP-04: Major third
T08-IP-04.desc: Chapter opening for Major third: 4 semitones, C to E.

T07-IP-05.title: Perfect fourth: 5 semitones
T07-IP-05.desc: Perfect fourth (P4), C and F, 5 semitones apart, 4 letter names.

T08-IP-05.title: Atlas chapter IP-05: Perfect fourth
T08-IP-05.desc: Chapter opening for Perfect fourth: 5 semitones, C to F.

T07-IP-06.title: Tritone: 6 semitones
T07-IP-06.desc: Tritone (A4/d5), C and F♯, 6 semitones apart, 4 letter names.

T08-IP-06.title: Atlas chapter IP-06: Tritone
T08-IP-06.desc: Chapter opening for Tritone: 6 semitones, C to F♯.

T07-IP-07.title: Perfect fifth: 7 semitones
T07-IP-07.desc: Perfect fifth (P5), C and G, 7 semitones apart, 5 letter names.

T08-IP-07.title: Atlas chapter IP-07: Perfect fifth
T08-IP-07.desc: Chapter opening for Perfect fifth: 7 semitones, C to G.

T07-IP-08.title: Minor sixth: 8 semitones
T07-IP-08.desc: Minor sixth (m6), C and A♭, 8 semitones apart, 6 letter names.

T08-IP-08.title: Atlas chapter IP-08: Minor sixth
T08-IP-08.desc: Chapter opening for Minor sixth: 8 semitones, C to A♭.

T07-IP-09.title: Major sixth: 9 semitones
T07-IP-09.desc: Major sixth (M6), C and A, 9 semitones apart, 6 letter names.

T08-IP-09.title: Atlas chapter IP-09: Major sixth
T08-IP-09.desc: Chapter opening for Major sixth: 9 semitones, C to A.

T07-IP-10.title: Minor seventh: 10 semitones
T07-IP-10.desc: Minor seventh (m7), C and B♭, 10 semitones apart, 7 letter names.

T08-IP-10.title: Atlas chapter IP-10: Minor seventh
T08-IP-10.desc: Chapter opening for Minor seventh: 10 semitones, C to B♭.

T07-IP-11.title: Major seventh: 11 semitones
T07-IP-11.desc: Major seventh (M7), C and B, 11 semitones apart, 7 letter names.

T08-IP-11.title: Atlas chapter IP-11: Major seventh
T08-IP-11.desc: Chapter opening for Major seventh: 11 semitones, C to B.

T07-IP-12.title: Perfect octave: 12 semitones
T07-IP-12.desc: Perfect octave (P8), C and C, 12 semitones apart, 8 letter names.

T08-IP-12.title: Atlas chapter IP-12: Perfect octave
T08-IP-12.desc: Chapter opening for Perfect octave: 12 semitones, C to C.

T01-native.title: How to read an interval card
T01-native.desc: Example card: Major third, C and E, 4 semitones. Numbered notes: 1 the name, 2 the two notes, 3 the keyboard with hops, 4 the semitone count.

D08-native.title: A first Interval Palette card
D08-native.desc: Major third: C and E, 4 semitones. The palette holds 13 cards and 13 chapters.

T04-native.title: Letters versus semitone hops
T04-native.desc: C to E uses three letter names (C D E) but spans four semitones. B to F uses five letter names (B C D E F) but spans six semitones.

T05-native.title: The tritone lens
T05-native.desc: Left: B to F from the Week 2 lesson, six semitones. Right: the Atlas card Tritone, C and F♯, six semitones. They are separate examples.

T09-ruler.title: Semitone ruler: C to C
T09-ruler.desc: Eight white keys C to the next C with twelve numbered semitone hops across the black and white keys: one octave.

S12-native.title: How to read our pictures
S12-native.desc: Five symbols: a glow marks the chosen home note; a ribbon is a voice; overlap is what is shared; solid is sounding and dotted is rest or optional; numbers on keys and timelines are the measurement. The size and colour of painted shapes are decoration only.

S05-native.title: Set up your own keyboard
S05-native.desc: A drawing of a keyboard with black keys in groups of two, then three, then two; left is lower and right is higher. A generic volume knob and three steps: choose a gentle sound, set a comfortable volume, notice the black-key groups.

X07-native.title: Six enrichment categories
X07-native.desc: The six categories in every lesson: History Postcard, Behind the Sound, Ambient Composer's Notebook, Hear It in Real Music, Musical Worlds, Paint What You Hear. Each has a simple icon and its name written in text.

A04-native.title: C as home, with the white-key journey
A04-native.desc: C glows at the centre as the chosen home note in this exercise. Around it, in order: D, E, F, G, A and B. A dotted path goes out from C through each note and back home. Distance from the centre is decoration, not a measurement.

F02-native.title: Held C beneath the same melody
F02-native.desc: A 36-second timeline: the lower voice holds C throughout; the upper voice plays E from 4 to 10, F from 14 to 20, E from 26 to 32, with rests between.

F03-native.title: The supporting landscape begins to move
F03-native.desc: A 36-second timeline: the lower voice plays C from 0 to 12, B from 12 to 24, C from 24 to 36, under the same upper E, F, E.
